questions.prompt: Write 47 in BCD, four bits per digit.
questions.explanation: Each digit gets its own four bits: 4 = 0100 and 7 = 0111, so 47 is 0100 0111.

questions.prompt: A BCD word reads 1001 0011. What decimal number is it?
questions.explanation: Read each group of four as one digit: 1001 = 9 and 0011 = 3, so it is 93.

questions.prompt: Which group of four bits can **never** be a BCD digit?
questions.explanation: 1100 is 12. A BCD digit is 0 to 9 (0000 to 1001); the codes 1010 to 1111 are never used.

questions.prompt: An operator panel has four BCD thumbwheel switches (0000 to 9999). How many PLC inputs do they need?
questions.explanation: Each thumbwheel digit has four wires (worth 1, 2, 4 and 8), and each wire needs an input: 4 × 4 = 16.

questions.prompt: A thumbwheel is set to 25, so the PLC reads BCD 0010 0101. A program forgets to convert it and reads the bits as plain binary. What number does the program get?
questions.explanation: As plain binary, 0010 0101 has 1s in the 32, 4 and 1 places: 32 + 4 + 1 = 37. That is why a BCD input is converted (FRD, or BCD_TO_INT) before it is used.
